terms.statutory_reference: RBI National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Technical Specifications
terms.plain_definition: A 16-to-22 character alphanumeric reference number generated by the sending bank to uniquely identify a fund transfer across NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, or UPI settlement rails.
terms.merchant_impact: UTR is the single source of truth connecting an aggregated batch payment from your payment gateway (e.g. Razorpay/Stripe) to the exact credit line appearing on your bank current account statement.
terms.actionable_tip: If a transaction is marked as an exception in Finora, paste the UTR into the search bar or Linked Accounts tab to locate the underlying batch deposit within 2 seconds.

terms.statutory_reference: RBI Master Directions on Payment Aggregators & Merchant Acquiring
terms.plain_definition: The percentage fee (typically 1.8% to 2.5%, with a standard contractual baseline of 2.0% plus 18% GST) charged by a payment gateway or acquiring bank for processing electronic payments (Credit/Debit Cards, Netbanking, Wallets). Note: UPI P2M has zero MDR under current statutory rules.
terms.merchant_impact: MDR creates the fundamental spread between your Gross Processed Volume (what customers paid) and Net Settled Cash (what reaches your bank account). Hidden rate hikes or tier misclassifications leak 0.2%–0.5% of top-line revenue if unreconciled.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora automatically calculates contractual vs. deducted MDR on every transaction and flags discrepancies as 'fee_variance' exceptions.

terms.statutory_reference: RBI Guidelines on Settlement of Merchant Transactions by Payment Aggregators (DPSS.CO.PD.No.1810/02.14.008/2019-20)
terms.plain_definition: The statutory timeframe in business days ('T' being transaction date, plus 2 business days) required for captured customer funds to clear through the nodal escrow account and deposit into the merchant's bank account.
terms.merchant_impact: T+2 latency creates an 'in-transit float' where money is earned but inaccessible for working capital, payroll, or vendor disbursements. Weekends and bank holidays push real-world clearing to T+4 or T+5.
terms.actionable_tip: Check Finora's DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) gauge on the Cash Position dashboard to track your live transit latency and simulate holiday delays via the Monte Carlo forecasting tool.

terms.statutory_reference: Section 23 of Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (RBI Master Directions on Payment Aggregators)
terms.plain_definition: A special non-interest bearing bank escrow account mandated by the Reserve Bank of India that payment aggregators (e.g. Razorpay, Cashfree, PayU) must maintain with a scheduled commercial bank to hold merchant funds securely before payout.
terms.merchant_impact: Customer payments never touch the payment aggregator's own corporate balance sheet — they sit in the nodal account to protect merchants from aggregator bankruptcy or operational freeze.
terms.actionable_tip: When verifying settlement batches in Finora, ensure the originating bank identifier matches the verified nodal escrow bank of your gateway.

terms.statutory_reference: Visa & Mastercard Dispute Resolution Guidelines / NPCI UPI Dispute Rules
terms.plain_definition: A **Refund** is initiated voluntarily by the merchant to return funds to a buyer. A **Chargeback** is a forced debit initiated by the customer's issuing bank due to alleged fraud, non-delivery, or authorization dispute.
terms.merchant_impact: Refunds return the transaction amount and occasionally partial fees. Chargebacks incur an additional non-refundable dispute fee (₹400–₹1,500), freeze funds in suspense, and trigger gateway risk reviews if your chargeback ratio exceeds 1%.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora tags chargeback holdbacks separately in the Exceptions Queue with evidence document upload deadlines to help you submit representment proof before statutory expiry.

terms.statutory_reference: Rule 36(4) & Rule 88A of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017
terms.plain_definition: An auto-drafted, static monthly GST statement generated on the 14th of every month showing eligible Input Tax Credits (ITC) available to your business based on sales invoices uploaded by your vendors (including payment gateways for MDR fees).
terms.merchant_impact: Payment gateways charge 18% GST on their processing fees. If your gateway files incorrectly or delays GSTR-1, you cannot claim the 18% tax credit against your output GST liability, directly reducing merchant operating margin.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora automatically cross-references the 18% GST deducted on every settlement batch against your gateway's monthly statutory tax invoice on the Cash Conversion & Leakage panel.

terms.statutory_reference: Section 194C of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1961
terms.plain_definition: Mandates Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on payments made to resident contractors or sub-contractors for carrying out any work (including logistics, courier, warehousing, and advertising contracts) at 1% for individuals/HUFs and 2% for corporate entities, if total annual contract payments exceed ₹1,00,000 (or single invoice > ₹30,000).
terms.merchant_impact: E-commerce and merchant platforms must deduct 1%–2% TDS when paying logistics partners (Delhivery, BlueDart, Shiprocket) before settling vendor disbursements, otherwise incurring severe disallowance penalties under Section 40(a)(ia).
terms.actionable_tip: Use Finora's statutory withholding breakdown during Month-End Close to verify that contractor payouts have corresponding Section 194C withholding entries.

terms.statutory_reference: Section 194J of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1961
terms.plain_definition: Requires deduction of tax at source on fees for professional services (10%), technical services & software/SaaS maintenance (2%), royalty, and director remuneration (10%), where payments exceed ₹30,000 per financial year.
terms.merchant_impact: SaaS software subscriptions, IT infrastructure hosting (AWS, GCP, Azure India), and treasury advisory fees fall under Section 194J (2% or 10%). Deducting the wrong rate creates demand notices during statutory tax audit.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora audits operational expenses during continuous close to separate 2% technical service charges from 10% professional services.

terms.statutory_reference: Section 194H of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1961
terms.plain_definition: Mandates deduction of tax at source at 2% (reduced from 5% under Finance Act 2024) on payments of commission or brokerage to a resident, where the aggregate amount exceeds ₹15,000 in a financial year.
terms.merchant_impact: Payment gateway interchange and distributor commissions are frequently audited under Section 194H. Note: The CBDT has issued notifications clarifying that banking merchant interchange is exempt from 194H TDS when deducted directly by acquiring banks.
terms.actionable_tip: Verify whether your gateway agreement is structured as an acquiring bank arrangement (no 194H TDS) or third-party facilitator commission.

terms.statutory_reference: Section 194Q of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1961 (effective July 1, 2021)
terms.plain_definition: Requires buyers with annual turnover exceeding ₹10 Crores to deduct TDS at 0.1% on purchase of goods from any resident seller if aggregate purchase value exceeds ₹50 Lakhs in the financial year.
terms.merchant_impact: High-volume D2C and marketplace merchants purchasing inventory or merchant hardware exceeding ₹50L must ensure 0.1% TDS is withheld from vendor disbursements to avoid 30% expenditure disallowance.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora's month-end checklist tracks high-value vendor aggregate balances and flags threshold crossings before the 7th of the following month.

terms.canonical_name: Ind AS 115: Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Gross vs. Net)
terms.statutory_reference: Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) Notification / Indian Accounting Standard 115
terms.plain_definition: The statutory standard governing how Indian companies recognize and report revenue. Specifically mandates whether a merchant is acting as a 'Principal' (record gross customer price as revenue and gateway MDR as operating expense) or an 'Agent' (record only net margin).
terms.merchant_impact: Merchants must report 100% of the customer order price as Gross Revenue and report the 2% Gateway MDR as Finance/Selling Expense — netting them out directly on the face of the P&L violates statutory Ind AS and statutory audit guidelines.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora automatically constructs your statutory Gross-to-Net waterfall aligned with Ind AS 115, presenting Gross Processed Volume, Gateway Deductions, GST, and Net Bank Cash separately.

terms.canonical_name: Ind AS 109: Financial Instruments (Expected Credit Loss & Float)
terms.statutory_reference: MCA Indian Accounting Standard 109 (Financial Instruments)
terms.plain_definition: Governs the classification, measurement, and impairment of financial assets, including uncollected settlement float from payment gateways and aging balances held in suspense accounts.
terms.merchant_impact: Unreconciled exceptions older than 30–60 days cannot sit indefinitely on your balance sheet — auditors will require an Expected Credit Loss (ECL) provision against unresolved gateway receivables.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora's Exception Aging Buckets (0-3d, 4-7d, 8-14d, 15d+) give finance teams the exact duration breakdown needed to justify asset recoverability during statutory audit.

terms.statutory_reference: Treasury Working Capital Management Metric
terms.plain_definition: The average number of business days it takes for credit card, debit card, UPI, and netbanking sales to convert from checkout authorization into usable cash deposited into your bank current account.
terms.merchant_impact: Every 1-day reduction in DSO for a ₹10 Cr/year merchant frees up roughly ₹2.7 Lakhs in permanent working capital liquidity without taking high-interest credit lines.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora computes your real-time weighted DSO (currently 3.0 days) across all active payment rails and highlights banking transit drift.

terms.statutory_reference: Automated Recurring Payment Framework (RBI e-Mandate Circular)
terms.plain_definition: The automated process of communicating with customers and programmatically retrying failed transactions, recurring billing installments, or subscription renewals across backup payment rails.
terms.merchant_impact: Smart dunning waterfalls recover 40%–60% of involuntary customer churn caused by temporary bank server timeouts, insufficient daily limits, or expired card mandates.
terms.actionable_tip: Review failed checkout exceptions in Finora to verify if customer payment attempts were recovered via secondary rails or if duplicate debits occurred.

terms.statutory_reference: ICAI Guidance Note on Internal Financial Controls Over Financial Reporting (ICFR)
terms.plain_definition: A continuous audit process that reconciles three independent transaction feeds: (1) Internal Order Cart/ERP ledger, (2) Payment Gateway settlement reports, and (3) Bank Current Account statement credits via exact UTR references.
terms.merchant_impact: Prevents phantom revenue, detects silent gateway fee overcharges, stops duplicate payouts, and ensures 100% statutory compliance during statutory and tax audits.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora executes automated 7-stage 3-way reconciliation across all your connected rails, achieving a 99.4% value match rate.

terms.statutory_reference: Standard Double-Entry Bookkeeping Principles / Ind AS 1
terms.plain_definition: A temporary balance sheet clearing account used to record unallocated transactions, disputed chargebacks, or timing differences until the exact source and nature of the entry is forensically verified.
terms.merchant_impact: Balances cannot sit in suspense past fiscal quarter close. Trapped suspense artificially inflates current assets or liabilities and triggers audit qualifications.
terms.actionable_tip: In Finora's Exceptions Queue, click 'Mark Explained & Resolve' to generate balancing journal entries and clear suspense balances into verified revenue or MDR expense accounts.

terms.statutory_reference: Forensic Accounting Standards (FAAS) - ICAI Standard on Forensic Audits
terms.plain_definition: A mathematical principle stating that in naturally occurring financial datasets, the number 1 will appear as the leading first digit ~30.1% of the time, while 9 appears only ~4.6% of the time. Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) quantifies how closely your ledger conforms.
terms.merchant_impact: Automated Benford analysis instantly flags synthetic transactions, employee fraud, rounded payment tampering, or duplicate checkout bots without manual sampling.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora checks your active ledger against Benford's Law in real-time — our current MAD score is 0.0041, confirming high mathematical integrity.

terms.statutory_reference: Quantitative Financial Risk Modeling Standards
terms.plain_definition: A computational algorithm that simulates 1,000 independent stochastic futures by modeling settlement latency, seasonal volume variance, and exception holdbacks as geometric Brownian bridge paths.
terms.merchant_impact: Replaces single-point naive cash estimates with probabilistic P10 (conservative downside), P50 (expected median), and P90 (optimistic upside) cash projections, ensuring you never face unexpected liquidity shortfalls.
terms.actionable_tip: Use the scenario selector on Cash Position to simulate stress conditions (+3d delay lag, 50% recovery) and review your dynamic P10 downside liquidity floor.

terms.statutory_reference: Contractual Merchant Acquiring Service Level Agreements (SLA)
terms.plain_definition: The mathematical discrepancy when a payment gateway deducts higher processing fees than your contracted rate card (e.g. charging 2.3% on a corporate card when your contracted rate is 1.9%).
terms.merchant_impact: Silent fee creep across hundreds of thousands of transactions can cost growing merchants ₹50,000 to ₹10,00,000 annually if not audited transaction-by-transaction.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora flags every fee variance in real time, calculating both the base MDR discrepancy and the correlated 18% GST difference.

terms.statutory_reference: Ind AS 7 Statement of Cash Flows / Treasury Operations
terms.plain_definition: Customer funds that have been authorized and debited from the customer's bank account or credit card, but are currently in transit through gateway nodal escrow pipelines and have not yet cleared into the merchant's bank account.
terms.merchant_impact: In-transit float represents real earned liquidity that is temporarily locked. Accurately tracking float prevents false alarms regarding missing revenue.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora displays your active in-transit float on the Cash Conversion & Leakage waterfall and models expected clearing dates automatically.

terms.statutory_reference: Ind AS 109 Expected Credit Loss / Internal Financial Controls
terms.plain_definition: The progressive grouping of open reconciliation discrepancies by the number of days elapsed since the transaction date: Fresh (0-3 days), Delayed (4-7 days), Escalated (8-14 days), and Critical Stale (15+ days).
terms.merchant_impact: Items in the 0-3d bucket are usually normal banking float. Items lingering past 15 days have an 85% lower recovery probability and require immediate manual escalation to gateway ops.
terms.actionable_tip: Sort the Exceptions Queue by 'Aging' or filter for 'Critical' risk tier to clear high-aging suspense items before period close.

terms.statutory_reference: ICAI Standard on Internal Financial Controls (ICFR) / Companies Act 2013 Section 134(5)(e)
terms.plain_definition: An internal governance control ensuring that no single employee has the permissions to execute conflicting financial actions — for example, simultaneously ingesting bank feeds, manually writing off exceptions, and cryptographically locking period books.
terms.merchant_impact: Enforcing SoD prevents internal embezzlement, unauthorized manual ledger adjustments, and ensures external audit compliance for SOC-1, SOC-2, and statutory audits.
terms.actionable_tip: Configure custom role policies under Settings > Team & Permissions to test for automated SoD matrix compliance.

terms.statutory_reference: Companies Act, 2013 (Accounts of Companies) & Electronic Audit Trail Mandate
terms.plain_definition: The final step of the Continuous Month-End Close process where the lead controller signs off on balanced books, generating an immutable SHA-256 cryptographic hash seal that renders historical transactions tamper-proof.
terms.merchant_impact: Guarantees to statutory auditors, tax authorities, and board members that closed fiscal periods cannot be retroactively altered, backdated, or manipulated.
terms.actionable_tip: Complete all 5 statutory checklist items on the Month-End Close dashboard to unlock the 'Sign-Off & Apply Period Lock' action.

terms.canonical_name: Value Match Rate vs. Count Match Rate
terms.statutory_reference: ICAI Internal Financial Controls (ICFR) / Ind AS 115 Presentation Standards
terms.plain_definition: The **Value Match Rate** measures the exact monetary Rupee volume reconciled as a percentage of total gross transaction volume, whereas the **Count Match Rate** measures the raw number of reconciled rows regardless of size.
terms.merchant_impact: Finance controllers and auditors focus on Value Match Rate because a single unmatched ₹1,00,000 corporate transaction introduces 100x more balance sheet risk than twenty unmatched ₹50 UPI micro-transactions.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora highlights Value Match Rate (57.6% scope / 97.7% statutory) prominently on all dashboards to reflect true monetary risk.

terms.canonical_name: Payment Rails (UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, Cards)
terms.statutory_reference: RBI Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS)
terms.plain_definition: The underlying banking infrastructure networks that move money electronically between payer and payee institutions: UPI (instant mobile payments), IMPS (24/7 immediate settlement), NEFT (half-hourly batch settlement), RTGS (high-value real-time gross settlement > ₹2 Lakhs), and Card Networks (Visa/Mastercard/RuPay).
terms.merchant_impact: Different rails carry vastly different settlement latencies (T+0 for UPI autopay to T+3 for international credit cards) and fee structures (0% MDR on UPI P2M vs 2.5%+ for corporate credit cards).
terms.actionable_tip: Filter reconciliation tables in Finora by 'Payment Rail' to isolate gateway processing delays unique to specific card or netbanking channels.

terms.statutory_reference: RBI Guidelines on Regulation of Payment Aggregators and Payment Gateways (DPSS.CO.PD.No.1810/02.14.008/2019-20)
terms.plain_definition: A **Payment Gateway (PG)** provides the pure software routing technology to authorize payment transactions without handling funds directly. A **Payment Aggregator (PA)** is an RBI-authorized financial intermediary (e.g. Razorpay, Cashfree, Pine Labs) that collects customer funds into a nodal escrow account and settles net payouts to merchants.
terms.merchant_impact: Payment Aggregators are directly responsible for T+2 settlement timelines, dispute holdbacks, and providing statutory GST tax invoices on processing fees.
terms.actionable_tip: Verify that your payment partners hold valid RBI Payment Aggregator licenses and maintain escrow nodal bank segregation.

terms.statutory_reference: Payment Aggregator Risk Management Framework / Card Brand Operating Regulations
terms.plain_definition: A risk mitigation practice where a payment gateway holds back a fixed percentage (typically 5% to 10%) of a merchant's daily transaction volume for a rolling period (usually 90 to 180 days) to cover potential chargebacks, fraud, or customer refunds.
terms.merchant_impact: Rolling reserves lock significant working capital for high-growth, subscription, or cross-border merchants. Tracking release dates ensures held liquidity is collected on time.
terms.actionable_tip: Finora tracks reserve holdback batches separately in Linked Accounts and models their scheduled release dates in your cash flow forecast.

terms.statutory_reference: ICAI Standard on Internal Financial Controls (ICFR)
terms.plain_definition: A discrepancy between two financial feeds. A **Timing Break** occurs when both records are valid but cross settlement cut-off windows (e.g. T+2 float or weekend batching). A **True Break** is a permanent mathematical mismatch (e.g. unauthorized MDR overcharge, uncredited payout, or duplicate debit).
terms.merchant_impact: Treating timing breaks as true losses wastes accounting hours; missing true breaks leaks permanent company cash. Finora separates timing breaks from true breaks automatically.
terms.actionable_tip: Check the 'Aging' and 'Root Cause' columns on the Exceptions Queue to verify whether an item is a self-clearing timing break or a true fee variance.

terms.canonical_name: Continuous Accounting Close vs. Legacy Batch Close
terms.statutory_reference: Modern Financial Operations Best Practices / Ind AS 1
terms.plain_definition: An operational framework where financial accounts, gateway settlement feeds, and exception queues are reconciled in real time every single day, eliminating the stressful 10-day scramble at the end of each calendar month.
terms.merchant_impact: Reduces Month-End Close cycle from 10 days to 2 hours, allows executive leadership to see accurate real-time margins, and guarantees zero audit surprises during external statutory audits.
terms.actionable_tip: Review your daily MTD close readiness gauge on the Month-End Close tab to ensure books remain balanced throughout the entire month.
